q1_issues.issue: `During` is used for the surface preposition "of" in "every night of her first six months" — the instruction set restricts `During` to during/while/throughout and names `During` for a surface "of"/"in" as the single most common head error.

"first" in "her first six months" is encoded as the property atom (Member sk_period_1 first) rather than the `Ordinal` head the instruction set defines for "the first N", inconsistent with (Ordinal sk_night_1 2 night) emitted for "her second night" in the same parse.
sk_period_1 never receives a kind atom — its only Member atom is the property `first` — so a referent symbol appears in the output untyped.

"Norren was a Council member" emits only the PartOf link; neither licensed route for a modifier+head NP is completed — no fused `council_member` typing with its genus, and no head-noun kind atom of the non-fusing part-whole route.

q2_gaps: A possessed, ordinal-modified time-span NP used as a discourse referent and temporal frame ("her first six months"): no rule says how to type such a span, how to rank it, or how to attach a stated extent to it (Measure … duration is defined for an eventuality).

"every night OF <span>" — a habitual whose recurrence is bounded by a span NP: the frequency machinery supplies the slot term plus (Every e 1 <cycle>) but has no carrier for the bounding period, which is why the parse reached for `During`.
An interval boundary anchored on an entity/period NP ("from her second night"): Start/End are specified with structured calendar terms, not witnesses.

A past-tense habitual ("supervised … on every night"): the frequency section says the event stays unmarked while the surface-tense rule requires (Past e) on a finite past clause; the parse emits both and the instruction set does not adjudicate.

A past perfect with the bare adverb "before" whose anterior anchor is an event in an EARLIER sentence: the ordering test is stated sentence-internally ("the sentence contains another asserted event") but its carve-out is stated text-wide ("no other event in the text"), and the bare sequence adverb itself has no licensed slot — it is dropped with no gap recorded.

A non-Gregorian calendar date ("day 455 of Year 2"): (Day n) is exemplified as day-of-month, so a day-of-year ordinal with no month has no stated convention (and the seeded date-ordering rules key on same-year-month day).
notes: Roles, negation scope (the alone-depictive and the indefinite lantern both stay inside the strength-0 bundle), tense wrapping of the PartOf, coreference of "her"/"the Council", and the leather_case / keeper_family decompositions are all handled correctly. The weak area is the two time-span NPs, where an unlicensed-slot approximation was chosen over recording the gap.
